summary: Collects Channel Associated Signaling packages for the Media Gateway Control Protocol, covering R1, North American CAS, PBX interconnect, and basic FXO support. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: Old phone lines send signals along with the call. This is a handbook of how a gateway should handle several of those old signal styles.

questions: how do old phone trunks send signals
how does call setup work in cas trunks
subtitle: Signaling packages for old phone trunk types in media gateways.

tldr.problem: Media gateways need to handle old analog phone trunk types that use Channel Associated Signaling (CAS) to control calls. These trunks come in many variants (wink-start, immediate-start, FXO, FXS) with different signal timing and sequences.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC defines six CAS packages (MS, DT, BL, DO, MD, MO) that abstract the low-level CAS protocols into a common set of events and signals. The gateway handles timing-critical protocol details locally while the Call Agent handles higher-level routing and call logic.
tldr.outcome: Network elements can now support multiple old trunk types with a single unified MGCP interface, hiding the protocol details from the call control logic.

today: RFC 3064 is Informational and documents signaling packages still widely deployed in telephone networks for legacy PBX and carrier trunk interconnect. It remains current for implementations supporting these older trunk types through MGCP gateways.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
RFC 3064 defines six signaling packages for the Media Gateway Control Protocol (MGCP) that handle legacy analog telephone trunks using Channel Associated Signaling (CAS). These trunks, still common in telephone networks, use in-band signals and precise timing to control call setup, teardown, and special conditions.

The RFC takes an engineering approach called functional partitioning: the media gateway handles protocol details like timing (measured in tens of milliseconds) and low-level state machines, while the Call Agent handles call routing and higher-level decisions. This lets the Call Agent use the same call flows regardless of whether the trunk is wink-start or immediate-start, because the gateway abstracts those differences.
sections.plainLanguage: Imagine a post office with ten different mail systems, each with its own rules. Rather than teach the sorter about all ten systems, you hire a mail specialist to translate each system into common labels. The sorter only needs to read the labels.

sections.title: The Six CAS Packages
sections.content:
The RFC defines six packages, each for a different trunk type:

  • MS package: MF (multi-frequency) wink-start trunks, used for PBX DID/DOD interconnect and Feature Group D terminating. Supports incoming, outgoing, and bidirectional trunks.
  • DT package: DTMF and dial-pulse trunks with immediate-start or wink-start signaling. Covers wink-start and immediate-start variants for both directions.
  • BL package: Basic PBX trunks, DTMF and dial-pulse, either digital or FXS interface. Always bidirectional with loop-start or ground-start configuration.
  • DO package: FXO (Foreign Exchange Office) analog trunks, loop-start or ground-start. Bidirectional, used for basic PBX interconnect.
  • MD package: Feature Group D EANA (direct access) and EAIN (tandem access) trunks for North American networks. Can switch signaling types per call.
  • MO package: Feature Group D Operator Services Signaling (OSS) protocol, outgoing only.

Each package defines which signals the gateway accepts, which events it generates, and which can be audited to track call state.
sections.plainLanguage: There are six different ways old phones send signals: the packages are instruction manuals so the gateway knows how to talk to each type.

sections.title: Events, Signals, and Tones
sections.content:
The RFC distinguishes signals (commands from the Call Agent to the gateway) from events (notifications from the gateway to the Call Agent). Key signal and event types include:

  • Call Setup (sup): On outgoing trunks, a signal to seize the line and send address digits. Parameters include address, caller ID, country code, and signaling type. On incoming trunks, an event that arrives with the incoming call.
  • Call Answer (ans): Off-hook from the far end, indicating the call was answered and cut-through is established.
  • Release (rel, rlc): Release call tears down resources; Release Complete confirms the call is released and the trunk is idle.
  • Suspend and Resume (sus, res): On-hook and off-hook without releasing resources, allowing the called party to put the call on hold.

Signals can be On/Off (stay on until commanded off), Timeout (last a duration), or Brief (short fixed duration). Tones include busy (0.5s on/off at 480+620 Hz), dial (350+440 Hz continuous), ringback (2s on/4s off), and reorder (0.25s on/off). Tone parameters may be provisioned locally.
sections.plainLanguage: A signal is an instruction the call controller sends (like 'start the call'), an event is a message the gateway sends back (like 'call is answered'). Tones are the beeps a caller hears.

sections.title: Call Setup and Teardown
sections.content:
Call setup flow depends on the trunk type. For single-stage outpulsing (MS, DT, DO packages), the gateway sends off-hook, waits for a wink (wink-start) or proceeds immediately (immediate-start), then sends address digits. For multi-stage signaling (MD, MO packages), the gateway may send caller ID or country codes first with intermediate winks between digit groups.

The Call Agent can request specific events such as inf (Information Digits, to signal digit reception) or oc/of (Operation Complete/Fail, to signal when a timeout signal finishes or fails). For incoming calls, the gateway sends a sup event with no parameters; the Call Agent may then send tones (ringback, busy, reorder) and wait for answer or disconnect.

Call teardown initiates when the Call Agent sends rel (from the originating side) or when the called party goes on-hook. Hook-state handling differs by endpoint: on the originating end, an on-hook generates a rel event and releases resources; on the terminating end, an on-hook generates a sus event, allowing the Call Agent to choose suspend/resume or immediate release.
sections.plainLanguage: Setting up a call is like a handshake: off-hook, wait for an answer signal if needed, send the number. Tearing down is simpler: hang up on one end, and the call controller decides what to do.

sections.title: Glare Handling and Special Cases
sections.content:
Glare occurs when both ends of a bidirectional trunk try to seize it at the same time. On MF wink-start trunks, the gateway uses protocol-defined rules to detect glare and may reject the incoming seizure with a specific cause code (44) indicating the channel is unavailable. On basic PBX (BL) trunks, similar rules apply but are provisioned locally.

The RFC notes that E911 services and Operator Services have special requirements: sus and res events allow the operator to be notified of hook events without releasing the call, keeping the call active while the operator interacts with the caller. For rel signal, ground-start trunks generate a tip-ground release to the PBX; loop-start trunks ignore it.

The RFC defines off-hook events at a higher level than raw CAS to match Q.931 call flows. A sup signal combines off-hook with digit transmission, and the Call Agent needs not distinguish between wink-start and immediate-start variants because the media gateway abstracts these details.
sections.plainLanguage: Sometimes both ends pick up at once—that is glare, and the gateway uses special rules to handle it. Special calls like 911 let the operator stay in control without the call hanging up.

items.label: Call Setup
items.desc: Seize trunk and send address digits (signal) or incoming call arrival (event).

items.label: Call Answer
items.desc: Off-hook from far end indicating call answered.

items.label: Release Call
items.desc: Release resources associated with the call.

items.label: Suspend Call
items.desc: Called party on-hook; call may resume if off-hook before release.

items.label: Resume Call
items.desc: Called party off-hook after suspend, resuming the call.

items.label: Release Complete
items.desc: Trunk is idle and ready for a new call.
